title: Home Was the Easy Part
author: GatorVault Staff
excerpt: Home was the easy part. The first time somebody gets close is when 2-0 has to mean something.
takeaways: Florida is 2-0 because two home games never got close. That is why the record looks like a start. It is also why the record is not a test.
The Campbell flags did not cost them at 45-3. The same flags, and the same slow start, can cost them at Auburn if the game is still close.
Sumrall's feeling after 52-3 is the story this week. Auburn is where that feeling gets measured.
Stop the run or you have no chance. Philo has been enough at home. Saturday is the first time the crowd is not his.
Honest range is still 7-5 or 8-4. Saturday would be the first 3-0 since 2019. Florida has not won at Auburn since 1999.

sources.reporter: Buster Faulkner and Brad White Tuesday

note: Surgical pass Sep 15, 2026. Thesis inside recap. Auburn tied to flags. Not live. Await Charles approve.
body:
Florida is 2-0. That is what you are supposed to be after Florida Atlantic and Campbell. Both were at home. Neither game got close. That is why the record looks like a start, and why it is not a test. Home was the easy part. Saturday at Auburn is the first night Jon Sumrall's standard has to leave the Swamp.

They put 66 on Florida Atlantic because Aaron Philo (16-of-21, 275 yards, three touchdowns, one interception) and Jadan Baugh (14 carries, 160 yards, three scores) never played a night that could get close. Vernell Brown III caught six for 117. Eric Singleton Jr. left on an ankle. A building will take 66-21 and call itself ready. Sumrall spent the next Monday watching the snaps that would not survive a building that is not theirs.

What he saw was football IQ: knowing what the play is asking, the down and distance, when they speed it up, when to crowd a receiver and when to give him space. On 3rd-and-short a corner sat nine yards off the ball. That is too far. They took away the long passes and let FAU speed the game up. The interception was a catchable ball, not on Philo. Philo changed the play at the line when he needed to, and led. The win was real. The tape was the first sign that 2-0 could still be a disguise.

Campbell was the next home Saturday, and the first series made that sign public. Completions down the field, then a field goal, the kind of start Sumrall told the defensive backs not to get scared of. At corner you are going to get beat. Next play. If that opening lives at Auburn while the score is still a score, home has already run out.

What followed was home doing what home has done, which is the problem. Philo scored from the 3, Patrick Durkin hit a 28-yard field goal, and after one it was 10-3. Then Vernell Brown III took two punts back, 64 and 70, and caught one from 14, Dallas Wilson had the 40, and Baugh finished it from the 2 with 20 seconds left. Halftime was 45-3. Philo threw for 242 yards and two scores. That is what a night looks like when the other team cannot stay in it, and it still cannot tell you Saturday.

The second half is what Saturday can use. Sumrall put the backups in and the flags came with them. T.J. Shanahan Jr. on back-to-back snaps, a hold that wiped a Baugh run that was already a big gain, then a personal foul. Roderick Kearney picked up another. That is 1st-and-25, and in this league the drive is already over. Seven flags after halftime. One in the first half. Three in the whole opener. Up 45-3 those flags do not change the score, which is the only reason the building stayed loud. If they show up when the game is still close, they are how you lose, and that is the version of this team Byrum Brown and Jeremiah Cobb will actually get to play.

Late in the third, after the night had already decided itself, Baugh went 75. Last year his longest was 26 yards. In two weeks he has 296 yards and five scores on 14 carries each Saturday. Campbell stayed on three. The Swamp left with 52-3 and a 2-0 start it had not had in five years, which is what home buys you when nobody can get close.

Sumrall walked to the locker room unhappy on a night most new coaches would have pocketed, and that is the feeling that still belongs to this week. Happy they got the win. Not pleased with a lot of the rest. Second-team and third-team guys got a chance to prove people right or wrong, and some of them showed why they are not playing. Sumrall called the depth behind Baugh subpar. A guy went the wrong way on one run. Somebody missed a protection call. The starting offensive line was not awful and is not where it needs to be. They did not give Baugh as many rushing lanes as they should have. Year One in this building is a coach deciding, in public, that 52-3 is not the point. Freshmen have been here since January. Play that second half in conference and they are about to have a real rude awakening. Walk in like that and they will get absolutely embarrassed.

Monday, that feeling was still in the rooms because Sumrall already knew who it was about. It had cooled, and it had not left. When they rolled the depth of the roster into the game, they did not play clean football. Sumrall wants them to finish on the quarterback. He wants sacks. These games count twice, he said, overall record and conference record, and the last two weeks counted once. If he has to get anybody ready to play SEC football, they have the wrong people here. Jeremiah Cobb and Omar Mabson II are both over 5.5 yards a carry and have 265 combined. Byrum Brown ran for a thousand yards and 14 scores last year, physical, playing with confidence, a lot of time in this system. The spacing and the shots get everybody's attention. What kills you is the run. If you do not stop it, you have no chance. Home let Florida pick the terms, and Auburn is not built to hand them back.

They may also walk into that without Singleton and Oyebadejo. Both are out of the boot, both were very limited Monday, both questionable, and Sumrall will not promise either one plays. Philo is the piece that has not had to prove anything away from here. He is confident and not easily rattled. If he plays like he has played through the first part of this year, Sumrall said, he will give them a chance to win every week. That has been enough with this crowd behind him. It has to be enough in a building that will not help him.

If that Saturday is as close as Sumrall thinks it can be, Tuesday belonged to the two men who have to call it. Buster Faulkner has to take a quarterback who has only started at home and keep him clean when DJ Durkin's defense is playing with its hair on fire, fast and confident. Same preparation every week, no matter who they play. You are not just playing 11 defenders. You have the crowd. Faulkner said Philo is cool, calm, and collected. They will coach him through it.

Brad White has the other half of the same close game. He has to take a defense that just spent two weeks in the Swamp and put it in a fight that already knows its own offense. Auburn has been in Alex Golesh's system for years. Pace, tempo, skill, a nasty offensive line. Fist fight. Rock fight. Be ready for that.

Florida scored 118 and allowed 24 at home. Auburn does not play those two games, and the card after that is why a close one this week is not just Week 3. Florida has not won at Auburn since 1999. Ole Miss, Missouri, South Carolina, Texas in Austin, and Georgia in Atlanta on Halloween are still waiting. Two home blowouts do not change those. The honest range for this roster is still 7-5 or 8-4. First 3-0 since 2019 is what Saturday would be.

Home was the easy part. The first time somebody gets close is when 2-0 has to mean something.
